description: Irving, Texas-based integrated power generator and retail electricity provider with a mixed nuclear, natural-gas, coal and solar fleet. In October 2026 the U.S. Department of Energy agreed to lend it $4.2B to uprate output at three of its four nuclear plants, amid AI-driven power demand growth.

target: Humain Data Center Fund (via BSF Capital)
description: A $2.5B data-center financing vehicle being raised by Humain, the Saudi Public Investment Fund's AI company, and managed by BSF Capital (Banque Saudi Fransi's investment arm). Proceeds fund ~250MW (potentially up to 1GW) of Saudi data-center capacity built with Al Moammar Information Systems, shifting Humain's buildout toward outside capital.

Jeff Bezos's rocket and space-infrastructure company (New Glenn launch vehicle, satellites, lunar lander). In September 2026 it closed its first outside funding round — $10B led by Coatue plus other institutions, with Bezos himself adding $2B — at a reported ~$130-140B valuation, bringing his total personal investment to roughly $30B.

U.S. data-center and power infrastructure platform backed by SoftBank and OpenAI, building sites including a 1.2GW Texas campus for OpenAI and the PORTS-Pike Ohio campus hosting NVIDIA AI compute. NVIDIA agreed to buy an additional $1.5B of SB Energy pre-IPO shares (on top of an earlier $1.5B prepaid forward) ahead of its Nasdaq listing targeting a roughly $50B valuation.

Berkeley-based public superconducting quantum computing company (NASDAQ: RGTI). In September 2026 it finalized a $100M, five-year Other Transaction Agreement with the U.S. Department of Commerce under the CHIPS Act for quantum R&D (readout electronics, cryostat design, Fab-1 upgrades), issuing ~7.7M shares to the government as a minority equity stake.

Palo Alto-based public quantum computing company (NYSE: QBTS), the dual-platform (annealing and gate-model) quantum vendor. In September 2026 it finalized a definitive agreement giving it access to up to $100M in U.S. CHIPS Act funding to scale annealing and gate-model systems, in exchange for a minority government equity stake.

San Francisco-based AI-data company founded in 2019 by Stanford AI Lab researchers, supplying training data and reinforcement-learning environments to AI labs. Raised a $350M Series E at a $3.5B valuation (September 2026) led by Insight Partners and S32, with Alphabet's GV participating alongside Addition, Lightspeed and Greylock.

Two-year-old startup helping brands increase visibility in AI-search answers (ChatGPT etc.), serving clients including Comcast, Estee Lauder and Walmart. Raised a $180M Series D at a $1.8B valuation (September 2026) led by Sequoia Capital and Kleiner Perkins, with Lightspeed and Khosla Ventures also participating.

Oregon-based superhot-rock enhanced geothermal developer, incubated at Khosla Ventures, drilling into the Newberry Volcano formation (temperatures over 375C) aiming for multi-gigawatt baseload power. Raised an oversubscribed $135M Series B (September 2026) led by Centaurus Capital and Doerr Capital, with ConocoPhillips, Shell Ventures, Khosla Ventures and Gates Frontier participating.

AI-security company protecting models, agents and workflows across the AI lifecycle from adversarial attacks, prompt injection and supply-chain threats. Raised a $100M Series B (September 2026) led by Delta-v Capital, with Ten Eleven Ventures, Morgan Stanley, Microsoft's M12 fund and Booz Allen Ventures participating; total funding now ~$156M.

AI-inference infrastructure startup building a 'multi-silicon' inference cloud that disaggregates workloads across GPUs and specialized accelerators (partnering with Cerebras, Arm, Samsung). Raised a $300M Series B at a $3B valuation (September 2026) led by Andreessen Horowitz, with Microsoft's M12 fund, Arm and Samsung Ventures also participating.

Enterprise AI software company (founded 2023 by Matan Grinberg and Eno Reyes) building autonomous 'software factories' for self-improving code development. Raised $200M at a $5B valuation (September 2026, more than tripling from $1.5B in April), with Blackstone, Sequoia, Khosla Ventures, Insight Partners, NEA and Clearlake participating; total funding tops $400M.

AI company automating operations for housing (apartment leasing/maintenance) and healthcare, used by roughly one in six U.S. apartments. Raised $350M (September 2026) at a $4B valuation — nearly double its 2025 Series E mark — led by Andreessen Horowitz and Bessemer Venture Partners, with Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan and Sapphire Ventures also participating.

Maker of Devin, the AI software-engineering agent, founded 2023 by Scott Wu. Raised a $2B+ Series E at a $48B valuation (September 2026, up from $25B in May) led by Andreessen Horowitz, Accel, Founders Fund, General Catalyst and Avenir, with Altimeter among many other participants; run-rate revenue rose from $492M to almost $900M over the period.
